## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
  regressions to slip through in practice.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
  any other unclaimed path.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
below for why):

- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).

Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.

**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.

**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.

**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
correctly, 2026-08-25).

**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.

**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
  universal guarantee.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

## Test config files are Tier 1

`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js` are
**frozen** ([frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)). Do not modify them in a feature PR — config drift breaks every contributor's harness. Changes go through the Integration team.

## Quick checklist before opening a PR

- [ ] New component → has `*.stories.tsx`
- [ ] Non-obvious logic → has `*.test.ts`
- [ ] New user journey → has a `.feature` file (Playwright spec follows after Lead QA sign-off)
- [ ] `npm run test` passes locally

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see

is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. ## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

## feat(sfcc-102): PDP slide-out size & fit — size guide data flow + ZimmTable

**Jira:** https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102

### Summary
- Introduces `ZimmTable` atom (with co-located recipe, story, and tests) as the canonical table primitive for size guide content
- Adds `useSizeGuide` hook and extends `useContentful` to resolve size guide Contentful entries with cyclic-link protection, feeding data into the PDP slide-out drawer
- Adds `SizeGuideContent` partial (CM/IN unit toggle, measurement tables, size-fit prose) and wires it into the PDP `product-detail` page; adds `sizeGuide` + `sizeGuideTable` Contentful content type definitions

---

### Changed files

| File | Tier | Owner | Reviewer required? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/index.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |

| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/index.test.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/zimmTable.css.ts` | Tier 4 (squad-owned `.css.ts`) | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.test.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.test.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.test.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` | Tier 4 | Squad | No |
| **`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`** | **Tier 2** | **UI Designer** | **Yes — second developer review required** |
| **`scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`** | **Tier 2** | **Integration / SI Partner** | **Yes — notify before merging** |
| **`scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js`** | **Tier 2** | **Integration / SI Partner** | **Yes — notify before merging** |
| **`scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuideTable.js`** | **Tier 2** | **Integration / SI Partner** | **Yes — notify before merging** |
| `.claude/registry/components.md` | Registry (auto-generated) | — | No |
| `.claude/registry/hooks.md` | Registry (auto-generated) | — | No |
| `.claude/registry/pages.md` | Registry (auto-generated) | — | No |

---

### Required actions before merging

- Tier 2 change in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — a second developer (not the author) must review; UI Designer notification recommended
- Tier 2 changes in `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`, `content-types/sizeGuide.js`, `content-types/sizeGuideTable.js` — notify Integration / SI Partner before merging; run `npm run install:contentful` against a non-production Contentful environment to validate the new content types before merging to `develop`

---

### Notifications sent

- [ ] UI Designer notified of `theme/components/index.ts` change
- [ ] Integration / SI Partner notified of Contentful schema additions (`sizeGuide`, `sizeGuideTable`)

---

### Test checklist

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run test` passes (Vitest — covers `ZimmTable`, `useContentful`, `useSizeGuide`, `sizeGuideContent` pure functions, `productInfo`)
- [x] Size guide slide-out tested end-to-end in local dev server: opens from PDP, CM/IN toggle works, table renders correctly, unit conversion is accurate
- [x] Tested with a product that has no size guide linked — no error, drawer content gracefully absent or hidden
- [x] Tested with a product whose Contentful entry has cyclic links — no infinite loop / stack overflow
- [x] No console errors in browser during size guide open/close
- [x] WCAG 2.2 AA — `ZimmTable` corner cell `VisuallyHidden` renders correct accessible label for screen readers; unit toggle buttons have visible labels
- [x] `npm run install:contentful` run against non-production Contentful environment to confirm `sizeGuide` + `sizeGuideTable` content types install cleanly
- [x] No regressions on Add to Bag, size selection, or existing PDP panels

---

9088WSS261 - mens

1112XF26A1 - one size
0169FF26A1 - shoes

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added locale- and region-aware Size Guides with linked tables, unit toggles, fallback images and responsive layouts.
  - Size measurements can switch between centimetres and inches, including ranges and multi-line values.
  - Added support for grouped tables, labelled and unlabelled layouts, borders, and empty states.
  - “Find Your Size” now opens the relevant Size Guide from product details.
  - Added conditional Environmental Qualities content and Benefits to Shipping & Returns.

- **Accessibility**
  - Improved table semantics, headings and screen-reader support.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue_development_info
entries.description:
Get development information (PRs, commits, branches) linked to a Jira issue.

This retrieves the development panel information that shows linked
pull requests, branches, and commits from connected source control systems
like Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitLab.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: The Jira issue key.
    application_type: Optional filter by source control type.
    data_type: Optional filter by data type (pullrequest, branch, etc.).

Returns:
    JSON string with development information including:
    - pullRequests: List of linked pull requests with status, author, reviewers
    - branches: List of linked branches
    - commits: List of linked commits
    - repositories: List of repositories involved

application_type.description: (Optional) Filter by application type. Examples: 'stash' (Bitbucket Server), 'bitbucket', 'github', 'gitlab'

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

      "value": "Overview\n--------\n\nThis page documents the size guide configuration for Zimmermann's SFCC + Contentful implementation. Size guides are surfaced on the PDP via a slide-out overlay (see [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102)).\n\nThe correct Contentful entry is resolved by the PWA at runtime by combining two independently sourced inputs:\n\n1. `sizeGuide` — retrieved from the SFCC product record. This is a product attribute set in Business Manager (see [SFCC-312](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-312)). Examples: `Clothing`, `Kids`, `Shoes`.\n2. `locale` — derived from the **PWA storefront session** (i.e. which locale the user is currently browsing). This is *not* stored on the product. Examples: `en_AU`, `fr_FR`.\n\nThe PWA combines these two values to construct the Contentful lookup key and fetch the right size guide content.\n\nResolution Logic\n----------------\n\n| **State** | `sizeGuide` **source** | `locale` **source** | **Contentful lookup key** |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| As-Is (current) | SFCC product attribute | Storefront level - separate size guides enabled for US storefronts | `size-guide__{sizeGuide}` e.g. `size-guide__Clothing` |\n| To-Be (future) | SFCC product attribute | PWA storefront session locale -  We should have local size guides for US, France, EU, Italian, UK, etc. | `size-guide__{sizeGuide}__{locale}` → fallback to `size-guide__{sizeGuide}` if no locale entry exists |\n\n**Locale Fallback Rule (To-Be)**\n\nResolution order: **locale-specific entry → Clothing entry → no guide (hidden)**.\n\nIf no Contentful entry exists for the `sizeGuide + locale` combination, the PWA falls back to the Clothing entry for that guide type. This means all products continue to display a guide even before locale-specific content is authored.\n\nAs-Is: Clothing Size Guides + Few US specific ones\n--------------------------------------------------\n\nThe following are the confirmed allowed values for the `sizeGuide` product attribute in Business Manager.\n\n| **sizeGuide Value** | **Description** | **Contentful Entry Key (proposed)** |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Clothing: OP-4 | Default guide for womenswear / general apparel | `size-guide__clothing_op` |\n| Kids | Childrenswear sizing | `size-guide__kids` |\n| Shoes | Footwear sizing | `size-guide__shoes` |\n| Denim | Denim / jeans sizing | `size-guide__denim` |\n| Mens | Menswear sizing | `size-guide__mens` |\n| Onesize | One size fits all — no measurements, care info only | `size-guide__onesize` |\n| Jewellery | Ring sizes, chain lengths, bracelet sizing | `size-guide__jewellery` |\n| Belts | Belt sizing by waist measurement | `size-guide__belts` |\n| Gloves | Glove sizing by hand measurement | `size-guide__gloves` |\n| Clothing - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__clothing__en_CA`  & `size-guide__clothing__en` |\n| Denim - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__denim__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__denim__en` |\n| Mens - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__mens__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__mens__en` |\n| Kids - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__kids__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__kids__en` |\n\nTo-Be: More Localised Size Guides\n---------------------------------\n\nThe PWA will combine the `sizeGuide` product attribute with the **active storefront locale** (from the browsing session, not the product) to construct a locale-specific Contentful lookup key.\n\nKey pattern: `size-guide__{sizeGuide}__{locale}`\n\nThe example below is a reference implementation to validate end-to-end resolution:\n\n| **sizeGuide (from product)** | **Locale (from storefront session)** | **Description** | **Contentful Entry Key (proposed)** | **Status** |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Clothing | `fr_FR` | Displayed when a shopper browses the French storefront locale and the product has `sizeGuide = Clothing`. Uses EU/FR sizing conventions for general apparel (e.g. dresses). | `size-guide__clothing__fr_FR` | ⚠️ Example — content TBC with Zimmermann |\n\n**Open Items**\n\n* The `Clothing / fr_FR` entry is a placeholder to validate the resolution logic. Actual French sizing content (measurements, conversion tables) to be confirmed with Zimmermann / merchandising before the Contentful entry is authored.\n* In Contentful - can we handle size guide mapping to multiple locales? e.g. in the EU International Storefront we have the en\\_CH locale but we may want to have that storefront/locale follow the French sizing (tagged to locale fr\\_FR). So then ideally the content team have this “French size guide for Shoes” but then they can multi-select the applicable locales as fr\\_FR and en\\_CH?\n\nThis is a proposed size guide table from Ilaria, currently ticket on Tryzen’s backlog for current website. By having locale available as an attribute for size guide in Contentful, we can enable the content team to set up localized size guides like so:\n\n![image-20260804-035854.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384434178/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Clothing 0P - 4\n-----------------------------------\n\nAgreed with Dani to for now remove the Alpha sizing rows (S/M, M/L, S, M, L, XS, S, M, L) for now from the Clothing table - the new designs simplify the table. The content team can set up different versions of the Clothing table once that structure has been defined.\n\n![image-20260804-015117.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383156227/download)![image-20260804-015136.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384073730/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Kids\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-014951.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383123459/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Shoes\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-014614.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383385604/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Denim\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015427.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384303105/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Mens\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-032007.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383614989/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Onesize\n---------------------------\n\nPending with Dani - assigning onesize probably means we do not render a size guide.\n\nSize Guide Content: Jewellery\n-----------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015624.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383057957/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Belts\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015703.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384368641/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Gloves\n--------------------------\n\n![image-20260901-013004.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att461504514/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Hats\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-035814.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383483908/download)\n\nRelated\n-------\n\n* [SFCC-312](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-312) — sizeGuide product attribute configuration in BM\n* [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102) — Size guide UI / slide-out overlay (PWA)\n* [SFCC-304](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-304) — Contentful content types epic\n* Product Attributes — full SFCC product attribute set",

    49	      paddingX: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',

    51	      minWidth: MIN_COL_WIDTH,
    52	    },
    53	    // Spacer row inserted between groups in labelless+bordered mode.

    55	    spacerTd: {

    78	      td: { paddingY: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', whiteSpace: 'nowrap' },

    82	      table: { tableLayout: 'fixed' },
