entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__resize_window
entries.description: Resize the current browser window to specified dimensions. Useful for testing responsive designs or setting up specific screen sizes. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to get the window for. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

+  test("both buttons render at Figma's literal 12px target, not ZimmButton's shared 24px icon-variant default", () => {
+    render(

+    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: DECREMENT_NAME })).toHaveStyle({

**As a** Shopper, **I want** to view a size guide on the product page without leaving my browsing

## Acceptance Criteria (verbatim, customfield_10231)
1. Given a shopper clicks Find My Size or Size & Fit Guide on a PDP where Measmerize is not
   configured for the product, when the link is clicked, then a slide-out overlay opens without
   navigating away from the PDP.
2. Given the size guide slide-out is open, when the shopper views it, then size & fit guide
   description (mandatory) and the conversion tables (optional, can be up to 3 tables: Size
   Conversions, Body Measurements, and Garment Measurements) appropriate to the selected product
   type are displayed.

   all measurements update to reflect the selected unit.
4. Given size guide content has been updated in Contentful for a product type, when the shopper
   opens the size guide slide-out, then the updated content is displayed without requiring a code
   deployment.
5. Given the size guide slide-out is open on any device, when the shopper views it, then the
   slide-out is fully responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
6. MOBILE-SPECIFIC: Given the size guide slide-out is open on a mobile device, when the shopper
   views it, then the table is partially displayed and the sizes on the most righthand side of the
   table peek out so that the shopper knows they can scroll to the right.

  fallback to `size-guide__{sizeGuide}`.

# Review — PR #113 (SFCC-102 PDP Size Guide slide-out), author JhoanDelaCruz
Reviewer: Marcel Navarro (FED Lead). Started 2026-09-22.
Base 63855e6ee (= develop head = merge base). Head 60dc243ba. 22 files, +2458/-130.
PR state at start: OPEN, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED.
CodeRabbit APPROVED 2026-09-22T14:14:58Z after 20 threads, all resolved. No human review yet.

## Gate baseline (measured by me, both SHAs, local)
| gate | base | head | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| npx tsc --noEmit | exit 0, no output | exit 0, no output | clean |
| npm run lint | 1297 (1219 err / 78 warn) | 1293 (1219 err / 74 warn) | -4 warnings (improvement) |
| node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs | 6 unacknowledged | 6 unacknowledged, none in PR files | no change |
| npm run test | 105 files / 1536 tests | 108 files / 1599 tests | +3 files, +63 tests, all pass |
CI: Unit tests PASS, Storybook a11y PASS, Deploy Preview PASS (built from head 60dc243b).
Playwright E2E (localhost) SKIPPED, BrowserStack SKIPPED — neither proves anything.

## Findings (appended as verified)

1. [in-scope defect][CONFIRMED] sizeGuideContent.tsx:305 — the `overflowX="auto"` table wrapper is
   not an explicitly keyboard-accessible region. axe-core run live against the rendered drawer on
   the PR's own MRT preview: 1 violation, `scrollable-region-focusable`, impact SERIOUS, 2 nodes,
   at 375px; 0 violations at 1440px. Chrome 127+ keyboard-focusable-scrollers means it does tab in
   Chrome, but the region has no role and no accessible name, and non-Chromium engines do not ship
   that behaviour. The repo's Storybook a11y gate passed because the stories render wide enough
   that nothing overflows — the gate structurally cannot see this. Ask: tabIndex={0} + role="region"
   + accessible name. STATE: pending adjudication.

2. [in-scope defect][CONFIRMED] zimmTable/index.tsx:207 — row-label cells render as `<td>` with no
   scope; column headers render as `<th>` with no `scope="col"`. Measured live on the preview:
   clothing + mens guides, bodyFirstCells all `TD`, headerCells all `TH` with scope=null. For a
   real data table this loses row-header association (WCAG 2.2 AA SC 1.3.1). axe does not flag it
   (best-practice, not a violation), so the a11y gate passed. STATE: pending adjudication.

3. [in-scope defect][CONFIRMED] sizeGuideContent.tsx:200-248 — `NavItem` is a raw `chakra.button`
   with `borderWidth: 0`, bypassing the themed Button recipe. Measured via real Tab traversal on
   the preview at 375px: CM/INCH receive the UA default `outline: 1px auto rgb(0,95,204)` (browser
   blue) while the same drawer's Close and Next-tab buttons receive the themed
   `outline: 1px solid rgb(25,25,25)`. overrideStyling.md "One canonical styling surface per
   component type" says the theme config is the single source of truth for interactive components.
   STATE: pending adjudication.

4. [in-scope defect][CONFIRMED] sizeGuideContent.tsx:230,231,246 + zimmTable/index.tsx:177 —
   hardcoded English user-facing strings: `aria-label="Unit"`, `CM`, `INCH`, and
   `<VisuallyHidden>Category</VisuallyHidden>`. 11 locales ship; every other user-facing string in
   product-detail goes through react-intl. NOTE the VisuallyHidden branch is currently unreachable
   with live content (measured: every size guide's corner header cell contains authored text
   "Size"/"CM", so `!col` is false) — the code path is dormant, the other three are live.
   STATE: pending adjudication.

5. [in-scope, ask-not-assert][CONFIRMED] zimmTable/index.tsx — `labelless`, `bordered`, `subColumns`,
   `columnSpan`, `row.spans`, `row.isHeader` are reachable only from the atom's own story and test.
   Grep scope: all of `overrides/`, excluding the atom's own folder — zero hits. The only production
   consumer is `richTextTableToZimmProps` (sizeGuideContent.tsx:261) which returns `{columns, rows}`
   only. That is 2 of 3 render branches plus 2 of 3 recipe variants unreachable. JSDoc says they are
   for the gloves and hats tables — measured live, gloves and hats are authored as separate tables
   per group and already render correctly through the standard branch. AGENTS.md "Minimal changes" /
   conventions.md "resist speculative abstractions". STATE: pending adjudication.

6. [in-scope, minor][CONFIRMED] sizeGuideContent.tsx:23 — `TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = '48em'` retypes a
   value that already exists as `BP.tablet` in `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts`
   (which itself imports `breakpoints.md` from foundation precisely so the two cannot drift).
   overrideStyling.md "Cross-file shared values" + "The alias tier is a reference, not a second
   copy". STATE: pending adjudication.

7. [out-of-scope — CONTENT, not code][CONFIRMED] Contentful entry `size-guide__clothing_op`, table
   "Clothing - Body Measurements": authored values are inches while the toggle defaults to CM.
   Measured on the preview: CM shows Bust 31/33/35/37/39/41; INCH shows 12.2/13/13.8/14.6/15.4/16.1.
   Size 0 = AU 8, real bust ~84cm. Same shape on Denim (waist 23.5-31.5). Mens is correct (chest
   86-106cm) so the conversion code is right. CDA payload confirms `defaultUnit: undefined` on both
   clothing tables, so `initialUnit` correctly falls back to 'cm'. The schema's `defaultUnit` field
   would fix it and no entry sets it. Owner: content/BA, not the PR author. Falsifies the PR
   checklist line "unit conversion is accurate". STATE: parked — report to Marcel, do not post.

8. [out-of-scope — DOC conflict][CONFIRMED] Confluence 04.4.4 assigns `size-guide__{guide}__en` to
   the **US** storefront. In config/sites.js, `en` is **ZimmermannAU**'s locale id; US is `en-US`.
   Measured key filters on the preview: AU -> `__en`, US -> `__en_US`, UK -> `__en_GB`,
   USIntl -> `__en_CA`, EUfr -> `__fr`. So a US inches entry authored per the doc would be picked
   up by AU and missed by US. Mitigated today only because the live entry links all 11 regions and
   `pickMostSpecificByRegion` filters on siteId. Owner: BA / doc owner. STATE: parked.

9. [out-of-scope — pre-existing][CONFIRMED] `resolveLinkedAssets` (useContentful.ts, NOT in this
   diff — already on develop) drops unresolved Entry links from arrays. If every `regions` link on
   an entry were unpublished, `regions` becomes `[]` and `isEligible` treats the entry as global —
   fail-open. Measured: the live clothing entry links 11 regions, only 8 resolve in `includes`, and
   the 3 unresolved are silently dropped. Not this PR's code. STATE: parked.

10. [not a finding — withdrawn] Hooks called after the `if (isProductError) throw` block in
    product-detail/index.tsx. Checked base: the same pattern already exists on develop (useState,
    useVariant, useEffect, useWishList, useToast, useCallback all sit after it). Inherited, not new.
    WITHDRAWN before presentation.

11. [not a finding — withdrawn] `useMultiSite` imported from the SFCC base path. Checked: no
    `overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` exists, so overrideStyling.md's Storybook/Vitest
    resolution trap does not apply. WITHDRAWN.

12. [not a finding — withdrawn] "EU-FR storefront renders no size guide." First probe showed empty.
    Re-probed: a country/language mismatch modal was intercepting the click. The CDA payload shows
    ZimmermannEUfr is in the entry's regions. Tool artifact. WITHDRAWN.

13. [not a finding — withdrawn] "CM/INCH buttons have no visible focus ring." First measured via
    JS .focus() which does not trigger :focus-visible in Chromium — reported outline-style: none.
    Re-measured with real Tab: a ring IS present. The surviving, narrower fact is finding 3
    (wrong ring, not missing ring). WITHDRAWN as stated; replaced by 3.
EOF

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_design_context
entries.description:
Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. 

IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. 

NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions.

Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__search_design_system
entries.description: Search for design system assets (components, variables, and styles). Returns matching assets from all design libraries. Use this when you need to find specific components, variables (e.g. colors, spacing tokens), or styles from design libraries. For new calls, pass `queries` as an array of objects, never strings. Each object must contain `entity` (`"component"`, `"variable"`, or `"style"`) and a string `query`. Example: `{"fileKey":"<file key>","queries":[{"entity":"component","query":"button"},{"entity":"variable","query":"surface"}]}`. Do not pass `{"queries":["button"]}`. Combine searches already required for the task in one call, without speculative terms, synonyms, variants, or checklist items. Results are keyed by query text. Provide either `query` or `queries`, not both.

query.description: DEPRECATED: use `queries` with one object entry. A text query describing one design-system asset to find. Use a specific component, variable, or style name, or a short natural-language phrase. Multi-word names and phrases are allowed. Each query MUST express exactly one search intent. You MUST NOT combine alternatives, synonyms, or unrelated searches in one query; this tool does NOT apply OR semantics. To run several independent searches, pass them as separate object entries in `queries` instead of making one call each.

queries.description: Array of search objects. Each entry must specify `entity` as exactly "component", "variable", or "style" (singular), and `query` as a string. Example: [{"entity":"component","query":"button"}]. Deprecated top-level `includeComponents`, `includeVariables`, and `includeStyles` do not replace the required `entity` in each entry. Run multiple design-system searches in one call instead of issuing separate calls per term. Each entry must be an asset already identified as needed for the current task, exactly as `query` would be. Do not add speculative terms, generic checklists, synonyms, or naming variants to fill a batch. Use one batched call instead of parallel tool calls. Inspect results before deciding on a follow-up, and do not treat an empty result as a reason to try alternate terms. Provide EITHER query OR queries, not both. Results are returned in the same order as the entries.

entity.description: Required asset type for this entry: exactly "component", "variable", or "style" (singular).

query.description: Text query describing one design-system asset of the specified entity type to find.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether to disable Code Connect for search results.

includeComponents.description: DEPRECATED: use `queries` entries with `entity: "component"` instead. Controls whether legacy top-level `query` calls include components. Defaults to true. Ignored when using `queries`.

includeVariables.description: DEPRECATED: use `queries` entries with `entity: "variable"` instead. Controls whether legacy top-level `query` calls include variables. Defaults to true. Ignored when using `queries`.

includeStyles.description: DEPRECATED: use `queries` entries with `entity: "style"` instead. Controls whether legacy top-level `query` calls include styles. Defaults to true. Ignored when using `queries`.

includeLibraryKeys.description: Optional list of library keys to restrict the search to. When provided, only results from these libraries are returned. Library keys are returned in previous search results.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__whoami
entries.description: Returns the authenticated user's handle, email, all the plans the user belongs to (and the ID for each plan) and their seats on those plans. You MUST use this tool if you are experiencing file access/permission issues or are being rate limited by the Figma MCP to help debug the issue.

entries.description:
Get all images attached to a Jira issue as inline image content.

Filters attachments to images only (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, BMP)
and returns them as base64-encoded ImageContent that clients can
render directly. Non-image attachments are excluded.

Files with ambiguous MIME types (application/octet-stream) are
detected by filename extension as a fallback. Images larger than
50 MB are skipped with an error entry in the summary.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.

Returns:
    A list with a text summary followed by one ImageContent per
    successfully downloaded image.

issue_key.description: Jira issue key (e.g., 'PROJ-123'). Returns image attachments as inline ImageContent for LLM vision.

content.text:
All four reviewers are still running. Here's what I've personally measured so far, so you can contradict anything that doesn't reproduce on your machine before it hardens into a comment.

## Interim — PR #113, SFCC-102 (Jhoan)

**PR state right now:** OPEN, `BLOCKED`, `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. CodeRabbit approved at 14:14 today after 20 threads, all resolved. No human has reviewed. Head `60dc243b`, and the MRT preview was built from exactly that SHA, so what I'm looking at is the real thing.

### Gates — head vs base (base = develop head = merge base, nothing has moved)

| Gate | Base | Head | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | fine |
| `npm run lint` | 1297 (1219 err / 78 warn) | 1293 (1219 err / **74** warn) | **4 fewer warnings** — he fixed some |
| `audit:tokens` | 6 unacknowledged | 6 unacknowledged, **none in his files** | no change |
| `npm run test` | 105 files / 1536 tests | 108 files / **1599** tests | +3 files, +63 tests, all pass |

Both `lint` and `audit:tokens` exit non-zero on a clean tree, so the exit codes mean nothing; the counts do. Unit tests and the Storybook a11y job genuinely ran. **Playwright and BrowserStack were skipped, not run** — the green tick next to them proves nothing.

### The one that matters most

**The Contentful schema he wrote and the renderer he wrote disagree, and content disappears silently.**

`sizeGuideTable.js:7-21` enables bulleted lists, numbered lists, blockquote, and embedded entries in the rich-text field. `sizeGuideContent.tsx:341` returns `null` for every node type except headings and paragraphs. So an editor who writes the "how to measure" instructions as a bulleted list — which is the obvious way to write them, and the Hats and Gloves guides already carry exactly that copy as prose — publishes it and the PDP shows a blank gap. No error. The section survives the empty-section filter because the text extractor does see the list's words; only the renderer doesn't.

Fix is either narrow the schema to what the renderer handles, or handle list nodes. His call which.

### Browser-verified, on the preview

1. **Keyboard access to the scrollable tables.** I ran axe-core against the live drawer: **1 serious violation at 375px (`scrollable-region-focusable`, 2 nodes), 0 violations at 1440px.** The Storybook a11y gate passed because the stories render wide enough that nothing overflows, so the gate structurally cannot see this. Chrome 127+ makes scrollers tabbable anyway, so it does work in Chrome, but the region has no role and no name, and Safari and Firefox don't ship that behaviour. Fix is `tabIndex={0}` + `role="region"` + a name on one Box.

2. **Row labels are `<td>`, not `<th scope="row">`.** Measured on clothing and mens: every body row's first cell is a plain `TD`, and the column `TH`s have no `scope`. A screen reader user hears "33" with nothing tying it to Bust. axe doesn't flag this (best practice, not a violation), which is why the gate was happy.

3. **The CM/INCH buttons get the browser's default blue focus ring** (`1px auto rgb(0,95,204)`) while the same drawer's Close and tab buttons get the site's dark one (`1px solid rgb(25,25,25)`). Cause: they're raw `chakra.button` with `borderWidth: 0` instead of the themed Button. Verified with real Tab traversal — my first measurement used JS `.focus()` and wrongly reported no ring at all, so I threw that reading away.

4. **AC6 (mobile peek) does work.** At 375px the tables overflow by 249px and scroll, with a 72px white fade on the right edge. One wrinkle: at exactly 768px the table still overflows by 10px but the fade is switched off by the `48em` media query. Ten pixels, so I'd leave it.

### Four things I found that are real but are *not* his to fix

- **The clothing and denim body-measurement numbers are wrong on the live site.** CM shows Bust 31/33/35/37/39/41. The reference image on SFCC-102 says CM should be 79/84/89/94/99/104. The content is authored in inches under a CM label, so the INCH toggle then converts it again and shows 12.2. Mens is correct (chest 86-106cm), which proves the conversion code is right. The schema has a `defaultUnit` field that would fix it and no entry sets it. **Content team, not Jhoan** — but his PR checklist ticks "unit conversion is accurate", and that claim doesn't survive the preview.
- **Confluence 04.4.4 assigns `size-guide__{guide}__en` to the US storefront. In `config/sites.js`, `en` is Australia.** Measured key lookups: AU sends `__en`, US sends `__en_US`, UK `__en_GB`, USIntl `__en_CA`, EU-FR `__fr`. A US inches entry authored per that doc would land on the AU storefront and miss the US. It only doesn't bite today because the live entry links all 11 regions.
- **The "Find My Size" CTA still opens a "Coming Soon" panel.** He redirected `onFindYourSizeClick` to the size guide tab, but there's a second, separate Find My Size trigger that still goes to the placeholder tab. The ticket contradicts itself here: the description says that link shouldn't appear at all for non-Measmerize products, the AC says clicking it should open the slide-out. That's a BA question.
- **The tab reads "SIZE GUIDE"; the design reads "SIZE & FIT".** Pre-existing label from SFCC-736/195, not in this diff.

### Three findings I killed before they reached you

"EU-FR renders no size guide" was a country-mismatch modal intercepting my click. "No focus ring at all" was a `.focus()` artifact. "Hooks called after a conditional throw" is already on develop. All three are recorded as withdrawn in the findings file.

### On Figma

You told me to find the nodes myself. **I couldn't, and I'm not going to guess one.** The Figma MCP lists a single page on `Zimmermann_Designs` that returns an empty 0×0 canvas, and a design-system search for "size guide table" came back with `PLP Bar Mobile` and `WishlistOLD`. So I used SFCC-102's own embedded reference image instead. That was enough to confirm the CM/inches bug outright, and it matches on striping, header rule, toggle placement and layout. It is **not** enough for spacing values, the type ramp, hover/focus/disabled states, tablet, or the grouped "Layout 3" table variant the code names in a comment. Those stay unverified.

Findings file is at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-102/review-pr113.md`, written as I went.

<result>## Scale line

I was dispatched one angle only — **data contract fidelity and failure modes** (the 5 sub-items in my brief: schema/consumption fidelity, TS type fidelity, failure-mode tracing, security, migration/install). I ran all 5, plus one live repro script (executed the real `resolveLinkedAssets` against a fabricated response) to convert a hypothesis into a confirmed crash. I did not touch styling, accessibility, AC-compliance-in-general, or re-run the four gates in `gates.md` — none of my findings rest on those numbers, so per the instruction to re-run only what I depend on, I didn't need to and didn't. I stayed out of other reviewers' lanes (no styling/token/a11y commentary beyond what's needed to explain a data-contract finding).

---

## Finding 1 — `unique: true` on `sizeGuide.key` makes the PR's own region-override feature impossible to author

`scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js:24`:
```js
validations: [{ regexp: { pattern: '^size-guide__[a-z0-9_]+(__[a-z]{2}_[A-Z]{2})?$' } }, { unique: true }],
```
`unique: true` on a non-localized field is a content-type-wide constraint in Contentful — no two entries of `sizeGuide` may ever share a `key` value, full stop, with no per-region carve-out.

But `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts`'s `pickMostSpecificByRegion` resolution — and its own test suite — requires exactly that: two entries sharing one `key`, differentiated only by `regions`. `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.test.ts:161-162` (and again `:170-171`, `:180`/`:188`) construct `auEntry`/`globalEntry` (or `localeAuEntry`/`globalDefault`) both keyed `'size-guide__womens_dresses'`. The moment a content editor tries to actually create the second entry this hook and its tests assume is a supported configuration, Contentful will reject the save with a uniqueness violation. The regions-override axis this PR builds and unit-tests is unimplementable in the schema it ships.

Notably, Confluence's own resolution algorithm (ticket.md) never mentions a `regions` axis at all — only `key` + `locale`, two tiers. So `regions` is extra machinery layered on beyond spec, and it's the part that's broken.

- **CONFIRMED** (read the exact validations array against the exact test fixtures; also checked `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — it does not strip/transform validations before pushing, so this ships as-is). Not independently verified against a live Contentful space (no CMA token here), but Contentful's `unique` validation has no "except when grouped by another field" mode.
- 🔴 must-fix
- **ONE-OFF** — new content type, no sibling `regions`-scoped type (`footerConfig`, `headerNavigation`) has an analogous unique-constrained lookup key, so this isn't a repeated pattern elsewhere.

## Finding 2 — `imageFallback → asset → file.url` crashes when the linked Image entry resolves but its own Asset doesn't

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:412`:
```js
const fallbackAssetUrl = fields.imageFallback?.fields.asset?.fields.file.url;
```
The type (`ImageEntry.fields.asset?: ContentfulAsset`, `ContentfulAsset.fields.file` non-optional) asserts that once `asset` is truthy, `.fields.file.url` is safe. It isn't: `resolveLinkedAssets` (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, pre-existing, unchanged by this PR) leaves an unresolved Asset Link as a raw stub `{sys:{type:'Link',linkType:'Asset',id}}` — no `.fields` key — whenever that Asset isn't in `includes.Asset` (unpublished/archived/deleted after the `image` entry referencing it was published; Contentful doesn't cascade-restrict this). I reproduced it by executing the real `resolveLinkedAssets` against exactly that shape and evaluating the literal line-412 expression against the result:

```
Resolved imageFallback: { "sys": {"id":"image-1"}, "fields": { ..., "asset": {"sys":{"type":"Link","linkType":"Asset","id":"asset-missing"}} } }
CRASHED with: TypeError - Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'file')
```

No Error Boundary sits anywhere near this render path — a repo-wide search for `ErrorBoundary`/`componentDidCatch` under `overrides/app` found only `zimmAuthDrawerContent`, `checkout-redirect`, `confirmation`, `checkout/partials/payment`. Nothing catches this. No test/story exercises the unresolved-asset shape (`sizeGuideContent.test.ts` only covers pure functions; the `FallbackImage` story's fixture always has a fully-resolved asset).

- **CONFIRMED** by execution, not just static reading.
- 🔴 must-fix
- **UNIFORM** — `overrides/app/utils/resolveImageEntry.ts:24` (`const asset = image?.fields.asset; if (!asset) return undefined;`) has the identical gap: a truthy-but-stub `asset` sails past that guard too. This is a pre-existing, repo-wide contract mismatch between `resolveLinkedAssets`'s asset-branch behaviour and every `ImageEntry.fields.asset` consumer — not unique to this PR's approach. What *is* new here is a third independent reimplementation of the same "resolve ImageEntry → URL" logic instead of reusing `resolveImageEntry.ts` (already shared by `drawer-menu` and `megaMenuContent`) — a DRY miss on top of inheriting the shared bug.

## Finding 3 — Confluence's "no guide (hidden)" fallback isn't hidden anywhere; a Contentful outage looks identical to "no guide"

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1017-1040` builds `pdpDrawerTabs` as a fixed array; the `size-guide` entry has no conditional guard, unlike the `envQualitiesContent` tab two entries below (`:1068`, `...(envQualitiesContent ? [...] : [])`). `pdpDrawerTabs` reaches `<ZimmPdpDrawer tabs={pdpDrawerTabs}>` (`:1344`) unfiltered. For any product with neither a matching `sizeGuide` entry nor a `c_sizeFit` value — including ticket.md's own explicitly-open categories ("Onesize... probably means we do not render a size guide", "Hats content exists... but Hats is NOT in the confirmed allowed-values table") — the shopper still sees a clickable "Size Guide" trigger that opens to a completely empty box (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:429-449`, zero-child `VStack`). Confluence's stated fallback is "no guide (hidden)"; only the *tables-within-the-drawer* are conditional, the tab-trigger itself never is.

Compounding this: `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:63` destructures only `{ data: entries, isLoading }` (drops `error`), and `product-detail/index.tsx:978` destructures only `{ sizeGuide }` (drops `isLoading` too). A Contentful CDA outage (down/4xx/5xx/malformed JSON) is caught in `useContentful.ts`'s try/catch, sets `error`, and is then silently discarded at both call sites — rendering byte-for-byte identical to "this product has no size guide." No console log, no Sentry breadcrumb. This satisfies "fail independently" (nothing else on the PDP breaks) but blurs "content gap" and "system outage" into one indistinguishable empty state.

- **CONFIRMED** via source read (no `.filter()` anywhere between array construction and the drawer prop).
- 🟡 should-fix
- **ONE-OFF** (specific to this tab array), though the error-swallowing shape (`useContentfulEntries` callers not reading `error`) is worth checking against this PR's own other new call sites — I found none besides this one in the diff.

**Clean, for contrast:** unpublished/missing `sizeGuideTableReference` array entries are handled correctly — `resolveLinkedAssets`'s array branch nulls-and-filters unresolved/cyclic Entry links, and `useSizeGuide.ts`'s `isResolvedTableEntry` re-filters defensively. That section just doesn't render; siblings are unaffected. No finding there.

## Finding 3 — `convertCellText` silently fails to convert several realistic cm-value formats under the INCH toggle

**File:** `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:34-57`.

I ported the function verbatim into a standalone script and ran it (not just reasoned about the regex):

```
input="86—90" (em dash U+2014)   unit=inch -> output="86—90"      (UNCONVERTED)
input="86–90" (en dash U+2013)   unit=inch -> output="33.9–35.4"  (control, correct)
input="56cm–59cm" (per-number suffix) unit=inch -> output="56cm–59cm" (UNCONVERTED)
input="56 - 59 cm" (single trailing suffix) unit=inch -> output="22–23.2 in" (control, correct)
input="56cms" (plural typo)       unit=inch -> output="56cms"      (UNCONVERTED)
```

The range regex's dash character class is `[–-]` — en-dash and ASCII hyphen only, **not** em-dash (U+2014). Word-processor "smart dash" autocorrect (very common when an editor pastes from Word/Google Docs/Notes) routinely produces em-dashes, and Contentful's rich-text editor does not normalize this on paste. The cm-suffix strip (`/\s*cm$/i`) only strips **one trailing** occurrence, so a range where *each number* carries its own "cm" (a plausible editorial variant, since the content-type's own help text only shows the single-trailing-suffix form as an example, never prohibiting the other) leaves the whole string un-parseable by either regex and it falls through unconverted. Same for a "cms" (plural) typo.

**Concrete failure scenario:** shopper toggles to INCH (AC3: "all measurements update to reflect the selected unit"). One cell in the table — because an editor's word processor auto-corrected a hyphen to an em-dash, or typed "cms" instead of "cm" — stays showing raw cm-looking numbers under an INCH-labelled column, with no error surfaced anywhere. This is exactly the "non-obvious, costly to debug" category testing.md calls out for requiring tests, and it isn't one of the 20 cases the PR's own test file covers.

I also confirmed **non-idempotency**: `convertCellText(convertCellText('76','inch'),'inch')` → `"29.9"` then `"11.8"` (compounds a second, wrong conversion). I checked every call site in the file (`grep -n "convertCellText("`, 5 hits) and confirmed none currently double-apply it — so this is a latent trap, not a live bug, but worth flagging since nothing guards against a future refactor composing these calls.

**Verified by:** running a verbatim port of the actual function against 14 constructed inputs (real executed output, shown above), not just reading the regex.
**Severity:** 🟡 should-fix (em-dash/typo cases — realistic editorial risk, silent wrong-looking output, threatens AC3) / 🔵 note (non-idempotency — no live trigger found). **CONFIRMED** for both. **UNIFORM** risk if this exact conversion function is ever copied for another unit-converting field — it's currently the only cm↔inch converter in the codebase (I did not find a second one).

**Severity:** 🟡 should-fix (em-dash/typo cases — realistic editorial risk, silent wrong-looking output, threatens AC3) / 🔵 note (non-idempotency — no live trigger found). **CONFIRMED** for both. **UNIFORM** risk if this exact conversion function is ever copied for another unit-converting field — it's currently the only cm↔inch converter in the codebase (I did not find a second one).

---

## Finding 4 — `useSizeGuide`'s locale-key logic, and its entire test suite, are validated against a locale value that doesn't match any real storefront

**Files:** `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:49-53`; `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.test.ts` (15 of its cases hardcode `'en-AU'`); `config/sites.overlay.js:31,39-42` (read-only, not part of this PR, cited only for comparison).

`useSizeGuide.ts:51` does `const canonicalLocale = locale.replace('-', '_')`, and the JSDoc (line 27) states the format as `locale = {language}_{COUNTRY}`. Every one of the 15 `useSizeGuide.test.ts` cases calls it with `'en-AU'` — a plausible-looking but **fictional** locale id. The real locale ids actually returned by `useMultiSite().locale.id` per `config/sites.overlay.js` are:

```
ZimmermannAU   -> 'en'      (no country at all)
ZimmermannUS   -> 'en-US'
ZimmermannUSIntl -> 'en-CA'
ZimmermannEUfr -> 'fr'      (no country)
ZimmermannEUit -> 'it'      (no country)
ZimmermannEUes -> 'es'      (no country)
```

For the 4 single-segment locales (AU, fr, it, es — AU being the **home/default market**), `canonicalLocale` is just `'en'`/`'fr'`/`'it'`/`'es'` (the `.replace('-','_')` is a no-op with nothing to replace), producing a `localeKey` shaped like `size-guide__{key}__en` — a different shape than the `{lang}_{COUNTRY}` form every test and the JSDoc assume, and one that's never been exercised by any test in this PR.

**Concrete consequence today:** harmless in the common case — since nobody is expected to author a `size-guide__X__en`-suffixed entry yet (SFCC-674 is still "Ready for Review"), priority-1 lookup just fails to match and falls through correctly to the default key. But the "priority 1 beats priority 2" behavior — the entire point of half this file — has **zero test coverage for the actual production locale value of the home market**, and if an editor ever authors an AU-, French-, Italian-, or Spanish-specific override (a completely foreseeable future need, per the ticket's own fallback-chain design), this untested code path is exactly what runs.

**Verified by:** reading `useSizeGuide.ts` + counting literal occurrences in its test file (`grep -c "'en-AU'"` → 15) + reading `config/sites.overlay.js` directly. Not executed against a real Contentful entry for any of these 4 locales.
**Severity:** 🟡 should-fix (test-reality gap with a real, if currently dormant, behavioral divergence for 4 of 11 active locales including the default market). **CONFIRMED** that the mismatch exists; **PLAUSIBLE** (not proven) that it will cause a wrong *user-visible* output before someone authors a matching entry. **ONE-OFF** to this hook.

Related, lower-confidence note: the Confluence doc excerpt in the ticket says the US-domestic key is `size-guide__clothing__en` (language-only, no country) while `ZimmermannUS`'s real locale is `'en-US'` (which the code correctly turns into `..._en_US`). I can't tell from what I have whether "en" in the doc is shorthand or literal — flagging as an open doc-vs-code ambiguity, not a confirmed bug.

---

## Clean / verified (falsified attempts that did not find anything)

- **`resolveLinkedAssets` (useContentful.ts) — no regression.** Diffed base-vs-head byte-for-byte: only `buildContentfulUrl`'s and `useContentfulEntries`'s *signatures* changed (new trailing optional params); the Entry-link resolution + cycle-breaking logic the new tests exercise was already present at BASE, untouched. The extensive new tests in `useContentful.test.ts` are covering pre-existing behavior this PR newly depends on, not new logic.
- **`useContentfulEntries`'s new `enabled`/`include` params — backward compatible, verified not just assumed.** Grepped every real caller repo-wide: `zimmBenefits/index.tsx`, `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx`, `pages/home/index.tsx` — all call with ≤3 args, so both new params take their defaults (`true`/`2`), reproducing prior behavior exactly. No other caller regresses.
- **Fetch-gating / dependency arrays — correct.** Traced `enabled` transitioning false→true (product loads, `sizeGuideKey` becomes defined): `useEffect`'s dependency array includes `enabled`, and the effect resets `isLoading(true)` before fetching, so no stale "not loading" state and no missed fetch.
- **No stale-closure / round-trip bug in cm↔inch conversion.** Every call site converts fresh from `extractCellText` (raw Contentful text) each render — the previously-displayed unit's output is never fed back in as input, so there's no compounding-conversion path in the code as shipped (only as a hypothetical future misuse, see Finding 3).
- **Grouped-table classification (Rings/Cuff Bracelets vs. Hats) is correctly distinguished** by the `bodyRowCount === 1` condition — traced against the actual story fixtures, not just the unit tests.
- **AC6 mobile-scroll-hint gradient** is deliberately and correctly disabled for grouped tables (they stack vertically, no horizontal overflow to hint at) and enabled for standard tables (which have a forced `minWidth` per cell specifically to produce that overflow) — structurally sound, though I could not confirm the rendered pixel behavior (see below).
- **Cache-Control `String()` coercion and `errorStatus ?? 'unknown'` changes (index.tsx, unrelated diff hunks)** are functionally no-ops — a template literal already stringifies an `any`-typed value with no tsc complaint, consistent with gates.md showing tsc already at exit 0 on both base and head. 🔵 note: scope creep bundled into a story PR, harmless.

---

## What I tried to falsify

Ran a verbatim-ported copy of `convertCellText`/`convertCm`/`normaliseKey` against 14 adversarial-but-plausible inputs and printed real output (not reasoning about the regex) — found the em-dash/per-suffix/typo failures and the non-idempotency this way. Diffed `useContentful.ts` base-vs-head line-by-line to falsify "did this PR change shared resolution logic" — it didn't. Grepped every real caller of `useContentfulEntries`/`buildContentfulUrl`/`useSizeGuide`/`onFindYourSizeClick`/`onSizeGuideClick`/`'find-your-size'` repo-wide to falsify "is this hook/tab id used somewhere I haven't seen" — found the second, more consequential use in `PdpFooterLinks` this way. Cross-checked `useSizeGuide`'s locale assumption against the actual `config/sites.overlay.js` site list rather than trusting the JSDoc's stated format. Searched for a sibling Contentful rich-text renderer to determine whether Finding 2's gap is a repeat pattern (found none — it's the first).

## What I could not verify

- **Real rendered layout on an actual mobile viewport** — whether the "grouped" tables (no `minWidth` per cell) become illegibly cramped at narrow widths, and whether the standard-table scroll-fade genuinely "peeks" the right column per AC6. jsdom/Vitest can't compute this, and per gates.md Playwright was skipped on this PR — I did not run it myself either, since my brief was correctness/regression via source, not the visual-layout angle (presumably another tester's lane).
- **Live Contentful API behavior** — whether the `fields.key[in]=...&select=sys,fields` query string is valid CDA syntax, whether `include=3` actually resolves the full `sizeGuide → sizeGuideTable → imageFallback → asset` chain in practice, and whether querying with a locale not in the space's activated list (Finding 4) has any real effect on which entries come back. No live Contentful credentials were exercised — static review only.
- **Real Business Manager `c_sizeGuide` attribute values.** SFCC-312 is "Ready for UAT" and I don't have its actual value list beyond the ticket's abbreviated examples, so I can't confirm or rule out a category whose real value has a second meaningful numeric segment that `normaliseKey`'s single trailing-digit strip would wrongly collapse (e.g. a hypothetical "denim-32").
- **Whether Finding 1's gating ("Find My Size will not appear" when Measmerize isn't configured) is intentionally deferred to SFCC-101.** I grepped for any conditional/feature-flag logic touching `'find-your-size'` and found none anywhere — so today it's unconditionally live — but I can't rule out that SFCC-101's own scope already accounts for removing it later; I'm reporting the current state as-is.

## What Marcel is missing

The ticket text itself says Find My Size "will not appear" when Measmerize isn't configured — nothing in this PR or anywhere else in the repo implements that removal, so if this PR is treated as fully closing AC1, that clause is being marked done while it's actually unbuilt (not just deferred quietly — there's no ticket reference or TODO marking it as SFCC-101's job in the code itself).</result>

Everything else below is judged directly against AGENTS.md / `.claude/rules/*.md` as instructed. None of my findings rest on gates.md's tsc/lint/test/audit-tokens numbers, so I did not need to re-run any of them.

---

### Check 1 — Tier classification

**Clean, confirmed:** the PR's table correctly self-identifies `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` and the three `scripts/contentful/*` files as Tier 2, matching `protectedFiles.md` and CODEOWNERS exactly (`overrides/app/theme/components/` → UI-designer tier; `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` + `scripts/contentful/content-types/` → Integration/SI Partner tier). This is the one place I most expected a mismatch and didn't find one.

**🔴 must-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** — Tier 2 gate identified but not cleared. The PR body's own "Notifications sent" checklist has both boxes unchecked (`- [ ] UI Designer notified...`, `- [ ] Integration / SI Partner notified...`), and gates.md independently confirms "No human review yet." `protectedFiles.md`'s Theme Component Styles and Contentful Schema Definitions sections both say "notify **before** changing" — that hasn't happened yet per the PR's own record. CodeRabbit independently raised the same point on `theme/components/index.ts:108` ("Confirm the required second developer review before merge") — GitHub marks that thread resolved, but "resolved" ≠ "review happened"; the checkbox state and gates.md agree it hasn't.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — the 14 other files are labeled "Tier 4 | Squad | No" in the PR table. **"Tier 4" is not a concept this repo's rules define.** `frozenFiles.md` = Tier 1, `protectedFiles.md` = Tier 2, and CODEOWNERS' own section headers explicitly define "TIER 3: ... plain ownership, not a protection gate" — nothing goes to 4. The only place "Tier 4" appears in the docs at all is `protectedFiles.md:25`, describing it *pejoratively* ("rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission"). The real source is `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`'s `getTier()` (lines 207-210): it only recognizes Tier 1/2 paths and hard-defaults everything else — including CODEOWNERS-recognized Tier 3 paths — to the literal string `'4 — Feature-local'`. Concretely, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` and `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` **are** CODEOWNERS Tier 3 entries (routed to `@pwa-squad-a`/`@pwa-squad-b`), and I confirmed `develop` branch protection has `require_code_owner_reviews: true` with 1 required approval — so "Reviewer required? No" for those files is factually wrong, not just informal: GitHub auto-requested exactly those teams for real (`gh pr view 113 --json reviewRequests` → PWA Squad A, PWA Squad B, Tier-2-Approvers, Tier-1-Approvers), and will block merge without one of them approving. Nothing here defeats a real gate (the gate still exists and still fires independent of the table), so this is a documentation-accuracy problem, not a bypass — but it's worth fixing because the next PR that copies this table format will make the same mistake.

**Related, not a finding of mine:** `.claude/rules/squadA.md`'s frontmatter claims `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` for Squad A, while CODEOWNERS assigns it to `@pwa-squad-b`. This conflict is already logged in `overrideStyling.md`'s "Known gaps" as flagged-not-resolved, so I'm not re-raising it as new — just noting it's live on a real PR now, not just theoretical.

**Scope gap worth naming:** the supplied `pr113.diff` is missing 4 real files from the actual PR — `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages,utils}.md`. I checked: they're genuinely tracked (`git ls-files` confirms), and `gh pr diff 113` shows they're mechanical regenerations (`> Generated by node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs — do not edit manually`, just a timestamp bump + table rows). Nothing hand-edited, nothing in my angle. But I flag the absence because "verify every changed file" was the instruction, and 4 real files weren't in what I was handed.

### Check 2 — Hardcoded user-facing strings

**🔴 must-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.** Zero `FormattedMessage`/`useIntl`/`useUiCopy` in any of the three new files (`grep` returns nothing in `sizeGuideContent.tsx`, `zimmTable/index.tsx`, `useSizeGuide.ts`). Concrete hardcoded strings that reach a shopper or a screen reader:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/index.tsx:177` — `{!col && <VisuallyHidden>Category</VisuallyHidden>}` (English-only screen-reader text).
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:230` — `aria-label="Unit"`.
- `sizeGuideContent.tsx:231` — `<NavItem label="CM" .../>` (visible button text, not just an aria-label).
- `sizeGuideContent.tsx:246` — `<NavItem label="INCH" .../>` (visible button text).

No id exists anywhere in `translations/` or `overrides/app/static/translations/` for size-guide strings (grep empty). This is not one written rule sentence in `.claude/rules/*.md` — I checked, there is no explicit "no hardcoded strings, use react-intl" bullet anywhere in the rule files (only components.md's note on `useIntl`'s Provider-throwing behaviour). **So this is a demonstrated-precedent violation, not a documented-rule violation** — but the precedent is total and in the same file family: `product-detail/index.tsx` (7 `FormattedMessage`/`intl.formatMessage` call sites), `detailsAndCareContent.tsx` (2), `staticProductHeader.tsx` (5), including the exact same file this PR edits using `FormattedMessage` for an equally short string ("Coming Soon", `id: product_detail.accordion.message.coming_soon"`). `useIntl` is explicitly allowed from any component including leaves (components.md's Context-backed exception), so there's no structural reason this couldn't have been done. This ships English-only "CM"/"INCH"/"Unit"/"Category" to all 11 locales across 8 storefronts.

### Check 3 — components.md

Clean: named exports match folder names (`ZimmTable`, `SizeGuideContent`), props types are correctly named/placed at file-top (`ZimmTableProps`, `SizeGuideContentProps`), container/presentational separation is followed (`SizeGuideContent` takes `sizeGuide`/`sizeFit` as props, doesn't call `useSizeGuide` itself), the extract-to-hook threshold isn't crossed (`SizeGuideSection`'s one `useState` + one single-dependency one-line `useEffect` stays under it), and Storybook categorisation (`Elements/ZimmTable`, `Commerce/SizeGuideContent`) matches real sibling precedent I checked directly (all 4 existing `product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx` use `Commerce/*`).

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** `sizeGuideContent.tsx:87-100` — a JSDoc block clearly written to document `isGroupedTableNode` ("Returns true when a table should use the centered grouped layout... Uses `every` (not `some`)...") sits directly above the wrong function: `isHeaderRow` (line 102, unexported, already has its own separate one-line doc) is sandwiched between the block and its real subject, so `isGroupedTableNode` (line 107 — exported, non-obvious, imported directly by `sizeGuideContent.test.ts`) has no doc comment attached to it at all. components.md requires JSDoc on "any utility function with non-obvious behaviour" — the words exist in the file but aren't attached to the export they document. ### Check 4 — conventions.md (magic numbers/DRY/naming)

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (but a recurring temptation).** `sizeGuideContent.tsx:23` — `const TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = '48em';` with a comment reading "Mirrors foundation/gridSystem breakpoints.md" — i.e., the author knew the source of truth and retyped it anyway instead of importing it. Clean: zero `any`, zero non-null assertions in any new file (grepped directly); `type` used throughout, never `interface`; `import type` used correctly and consistently in every new file; `readonly` correctly applied to `ZimmTableProps`' array fields.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (pattern risk).** `zimmTable/index.tsx:15-40` — `ZimmTableProps` hand-rolls what is really a 3-way discriminated union (`standard`/`labelless`/`bordered`) as two independent optional booleans (`labelless?`, `bordered?`) plus a `columns: readonly string[]` field that is **required** but completely unused whenever `labelless` is true — confirmed by reading all three render branches, and by the `Labelless`/`LabellessBordered` stories having to pass `columns: []` for no functional reason. The component itself already computes the real 3-way discriminant internally (`labelless && bordered ? 'bordered' : labelless ? 'labelless' : 'standard'`) purely to feed Chakra's recipe — the discriminant exists, it's just not surfaced in the public prop type the way typescript.md's "Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling" section asks for.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** `zimmTable/index.stories.tsx`'s `Default` story (lines 47-53+) has a `play` function asserting only static content presence (column header exists, row label exists, cell value exists) for a component with zero interactive behaviour anywhere (`ZimmTable` has no `onClick`/`onKeyDown`/focus handling at all). testing.md: "If the story is purely visual... no play is needed," and the same claims (headers render, row label + cell values render) are already independently proven by `index.test.tsx`'s Vitest suite. - Assumed the PR's tier table would be wrong on the two "interesting" files — it wasn't; I verified against CODEOWNERS directly and it's correct. Reported as clean rather than forcing a finding.

## What Marcel is missing

CODEOWNERS' own comment calling Tier 3 "plain ownership, not a protection gate" is factually wrong against this repo's actual `develop` branch protection (`require_code_owner_reviews: true`, repo-wide, no tier carve-out) — every Tier 3 CODEOWNERS match is already a hard merge-blocking gate today, same as Tier 1/2, just routed to the squad team instead of an approver team. 18. [in-scope defect][CONFIRMED LIVE — highest consequence, found by me, no agent caught it]
    Toggling INCH converts only ONE section of a multi-entry guide; the rest silently stay in cm.
    Measured on the preview, product 0551XF26A1 (gloves):
      CM:   "Palm Circumference 18.9 | 21.7" · "Length 26.3 | 27.4" · "Length 61.5 | 62.6"
      INCH: "Palm Circumference  7.4 |  8.5" · "Length 26.3 | 27.4" · "Length 61.5 | 62.6"
    Only the first section converted. A shopper reads "Length 26.3" as inches; 26.3in is 67cm.
    Mechanism, confirmed from the CDA payload: the gloves guide links THREE sizeGuideTable entries
    ("GLOVES - SIZE CONVERSIONS" hasCmInchToggle=true, "Short Gloves" false, "LONG GLOVES" false).
    `SizeGuideSection` (sizeGuideContent.tsx:398-404) holds `useState<Unit>` per entry, and its own
    JSDoc states this is deliberate: "Each section owns its own CM/INCH unit state so toggling one

content.text:
Three of four reviewers are in and adjudicated. One update worth giving you now, because it outranks everything I sent earlier.

## I found a live wrong-measurement bug on the gloves guide

No reviewer caught this. Measured on the preview, product `0551XF26A1`:

| Section | CM | after clicking INCH |
|---|---|---|
| GLOVES - SIZE CONVERSIONS | Palm Circumference 18.9 / 21.7 | **7.4 / 8.5** ✓ converted |
| SHORT GLOVES | Length 26.3 / 27.4 | **26.3 / 27.4** ✗ unchanged |
| LONG GLOVES | Length 61.5 / 62.6 | **61.5 / 62.6** ✗ unchanged |

A shopper clicks INCH and two of the three sections silently stay in centimetres, with no toggle of their own and nothing saying they're cm. "Length 26.3" read as inches is 67cm. That's materially wrong fit information on a live page.

The mechanism, from the Contentful payload: the gloves guide links **three** `sizeGuideTable` entries, and only the first has `hasCmInchToggle: true`. `SizeGuideSection` holds unit state per entry, and its JSDoc says that's deliberate: *"Each section owns its own CM/INCH unit state so toggling one section's unit does not affect any other section."* So the one toggle that renders structurally cannot reach the other two.

Hats proves the mechanism by working correctly: it links **one** entry containing three table nodes, so one section, one toggle, and all three tables convert.

AC3 says "all measurements update to reflect the selected unit." Per-section state can't satisfy that for a guide split across entries. Two acceptable fixes: lift the state to `SizeGuideContent` and show one toggle per guide, or require the flag on every entry that carries measurements. This came in via commit `5e57f51e` ("per-table CM/INCH toggle"), so it's a design call to revisit, not carelessness.

## Two more that survived verification

**The schema forbids what the hook's own tests assert.** `sizeGuide.js:24` puts `{unique: true}` on `key`, so no two entries can ever share one. But `useSizeGuide.test.ts` builds exactly that pair — `auEntry` and `globalEntry`, both keyed `size-guide__womens_dresses` — to prove region precedence. Three of the five region tests validate a state Contentful will refuse to save. Region filtering landed in the last commit; it looks like it wasn't reconciled against the schema he'd already written. Confluence's own algorithm never mentions a regions axis at all.

**An unresolved Contentful asset crashes the render.** `useContentful.ts:76-78` resolves Asset links with `if (linked) ...` and **no else**, unlike the Entry branch right below it which deletes the stub. So an unpublished asset survives as a `{sys:{type:'Link'}}` object with no `.fields`. Then `sizeGuideContent.tsx:412` does `asset?.fields.file.url` and throws. The optional chain guards `asset` being absent, not `asset` being a stub. One reviewer reproduced it by executing the real function; I confirmed the missing `else` by reading it. No error boundary anywhere near this path.

## Where the reviewers disagreed, and who was right

Two of them contradicted each other on locale handling. One claimed `canonicalLocale` is always `{lang}_{COUNTRY}` so a bare-language key can never be produced. That's wrong — `config/sites.js` yields `en` for Australia and `fr`/`it`/`es` for the EU sites, and I measured AU requesting `size-guide__clothing_op__en` live. The other reviewer got it right and it matches the Confluence collision I flagged earlier. I've marked the first one unsupported.

## Three things I killed this round

`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` is **not** a Contentful rich-text renderer I could accuse him of duplicating — it parses HTML strings, a different thing. `.claude/registry/*` does **not** pull in a hidden Tier 1 requirement; Tier-1 Approvers were requested because the Tier 2 paths list them as co-owners, so his tier table is right. And the em-dash conversion gap one reviewer found by executing the function is real in code but doesn't hit any live content — hats' `56-59cm` converts correctly to `22–23.2 in`. Robustness note, not a defect.

One reviewer left, on styling and accessibility. Then I'll bring you the ranked set and the calls that are yours.
