<result>## Scale line

My brief assigned exactly 5 points (styling hierarchy split, token discipline, duplication search, deep table/control/scroll/image a11y, AC5/AC6 responsiveness) — I ran all 5, no more, no less. I did not fan out to sub-agents: the files are few (3 primary + cross-references) and the findings interlock (e.g. the token choice for a border colour informs the focus-visibility finding), so splitting would have cost more than it saved. I did not re-run `tsc`/`lint`/`test` (gates.md: those are the lead reviewer's, not mine) — I re-ran only `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` myself, once, because a finding depended on it. I went **beyond** reading source in one respect: for the "would axe-core catch this" questions, I built a throwaway jsdom+vitest harness (this repo's own toolchain, axe-core v4.11.4 — the same version installed) and ran the actual rendered markup through `axe.run()`, then deleted the scratch files. That extra step is justified because the brief explicitly demands a yes/no answer on axe, and reasoning-from-memory about ARIA-rule internals is exactly the kind of claim this task's evidence bar exists to prevent. I did not do live-browser/Playwright verification anywhere (no browser available, stated up front, applies to every layout/overflow claim below).

---

## 1. Styling hierarchy — where does styling live vs. where the rules say it should

**`zimmTable.css.ts` + `index.tsx`: clean, defensible split.** The recipe's own header comment states the intended division ("Static base styles... live here; conditional styles... applied as direct Chakra props... so branching logic stays in JSX") and the code matches it exactly: `zimmTable.css.ts` owns `textStyle`, `color: var(--zimm-color-text-default)`, `paddingX`, `tableLayout` per variant; `index.tsx` owns `borderBottom`/`borderRight`/`textAlign`/`colSpan`/`bg` as direct props because those genuinely depend on row index, column index, and variant branching that lives in JSX anyway. No bare Chakra token keys anywhere in either file — every colour/spacing reference is `var(--zimm-*)` (`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2), including `BORDER_SECONDARY`/`BORDER_FOCUS`, which are correctly centralised as exported constants (imported by `sizeGuideContent.tsx`'s `GroupedSizeTable` rather than re-declared — good DRY). **No finding here** — this is the part of the PR I'd point to as the reference example.

**`sizeGuideContent.tsx` has no co-located recipe at all** — everything (`NavItem`, `UnitToggle`, `GroupedSizeTable`, `ScrollableTable`, `renderTextNode`) is direct Chakra props + ad-hoc `sx`. Judged against the rules as written, this is defensible: these aren't a registered Chakra component type going through `useMultiStyleConfig`, they're one-off page-partial composition, which is exactly what hierarchy point 4 (`sx` for a one-off gap) is for. 🔵 note, not a finding: if a CM/INCH-style toggle is ever needed a second time elsewhere, it should become a real atom with its own recipe at that point, not before.

## 2. Token discipline

Re-ran `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` myself in `wt113` (HEAD): **exit 1, "6 unacknowledged violation(s) found,"** listed at `footer/footer.css.ts:20`, `zimmIconAndText.css.ts:7`, `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:22`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts:66`, `zimmBenefits.css.ts:4`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts:13` — **identical set to gates.md, none in this PR's files.** Semantic-category check (colour on `color:`, background on `bg:`, border on `border-color:`) across both files: clean, no mismatches — every `color=` prop resolves a `text.*`-derived var, every `border*=` prop resolves a `border.*`-derived var.

One real finding the script's own scope structurally cannot see:

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:23`** — `const TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = '48em';`, a raw literal duplicating the registered foundation breakpoint. The file's own comment says "Mirrors foundation/gridSystem breakpoints.md" — the author knew the source and typed the value again anyway instead of importing it. I re-ran the audit script and confirm **why it didn't flag this**: `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` line 10/132/139 hardcodes its scan roots to `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` only (confirmed by reading the script's `SCAN_ROOTS`/`walk` logic, not just its printed "Scanned 144 files" line). `sizeGuideContent.tsx` lives under `overrides/app/pages/**` — structurally invisible to the script regardless of content. For comparison, `zimmIconAndText.css.ts:7`'s own `BP_DESKTOP = '64em'` (a directly comparable raw-em breakpoint duplicate) **is** caught by the script precisely because it lives under `overrides/app/components/`. Same mistake, different visibility, purely by file location.
🟡 should-fix, **CONFIRMED** (ran the script myself + read its scope logic), **UNIFORM** (the audit-script blind spot is real for any future `pages/` partial, not just this one).

## 3. Duplication search

Grepped `overrides/app/` for the breakpoint value and the conversion constant:

- **`TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = '48em'`** (point 2 above) duplicates `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts:15`'s `breakpoints.md`. This is not a one-off oversight — I found **15+ other call sites** (`footer.css.ts`, `headerShared.ts`, `zimmIconAndText.css.ts`, `zimmDrawer.css.ts`, `zimmButton.css.ts`, `zimmTabs.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardShared.ts`'s `DESKTOP_QUERY`, `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/Rail`, `megaMenuContent.css.ts`, `leftBar`/`rightBar.css.ts`, `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`, `theme/index.test.tsx`) that all correctly `import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation/gridSystem'` and interpolate `${breakpoints.md}`. `footerShared.ts` is the closest structural precedent (a shared `BP.tablet = breakpoints.md` re-export specifically for files that can't consume `var()` in a media query) and this file didn't follow it. 🟡 should-fix, **CONFIRMED**, **UNIFORM** (established pattern violated by exactly one file).
- **`CM_TO_INCH = 0.393701`** — searched `overrides/app/theme/` and `overrides/app/utils/` for an existing conversion constant; found none elsewhere in the codebase. This one is genuinely new, not a duplicate. Clean.
- **`MIN_COL_WIDTH`**'s `calc(4xl + m)` formula — searched for the same calc pattern elsewhere; not reused anywhere else, no duplication.

## 4. Accessibility — table semantics, CM/INCH control, scroll region, fallback image, headings

I built a temporary vitest+axe-core probe (this repo's own installed axe-core 4.11.4, deleted after use) rendering the actual `ZimmTable`/`SizeGuideContent` components with fixture data matching the PR's own stories, to get reproducible answers rather than guesses.

**a) Row label rendered as `<td>`, not `<th scope="row">` — `zimmTable/index.tsx:207-209`.**

**e) CM/INCH control — `sizeGuideContent.tsx:200-248`.** Real `<button>` elements (confirmed via probe: `<button aria-pressed="true">CM</button>`), so **keyboard operability is fine** (native Enter/Space, no `onKeyDown` needed). Accessible name is fine (visible text "CM"/"INCH" satisfies `button-name`). The pattern choice itself — two independently `aria-pressed` buttons for a mutually-exclusive two-option control, wrapped in `role="group" aria-label="Unit"` — is valid ARIA (my axe probe against this exact markup: zero violations) but is not the WAI-ARIA APG-recommended pattern for mutual exclusivity (that's `radiogroup`/`radio`+`aria-checked`); `aria-pressed` communicates two independent on/off states, not "1 of 2 selected." This is a **best-practice/4.1.2-adjacent** concern, not a hard SC failure — name/role/value are each individually programmatically determined and do update correctly. 🟡 should-fix, **CONFIRMED** (structure) / **PLAUSIBLE** (real-world AT confusion), **ONE-OFF** (no other toggle like it exists yet in this feature).

**f) Focus visibility on `NavItem` — `sizeGuideContent.tsx:200-211`.** This raw `chakra.button` sets `sx={{background:'none', padding:0, borderWidth:0, cursor:'pointer'}}` and nothing else — no `_focusVisible`, no `outline`. I checked `globalStyles.ts` for a global reset that might remove default browser outline: the only `outline: 'none'`/`_focusVisible` rules there are scoped to opt-in `.zimm-*` classes (`.zimm-form-control`, `.zimm-focus-visible`), which `NavItem` never applies. So it likely still shows the *browser's own default* focus ring on keyboard focus — but not the app's branded `--zimm-focus-ring` treatment that every other interactive element in this codebase gets explicitly (`zimmButton.css.ts`'s `_focusVisible: {outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', ...}` pattern, applied consistently across every button variant I checked). WCAG **2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA)** — I can't confirm it's *invisible* (no browser), only that it's inconsistent with the established styling surface for interactive controls (`overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface per component type"). 🟡 should-fix, **PLAUSIBLE**, **ONE-OFF**.

**g) Horizontally scrollable region — `sizeGuideContent.tsx:305`.** `<Box overflowX="auto" sx={{td:{whiteSpace:'pre-line'}}}>` wrapping `ZimmTable`. Confirmed via probe (`hasAttribute('tabindex')` → `false`, `hasAttribute('role')` → `false`, no `aria-label`) — no keyboard affordance at all. This maps directly to axe's real rule `scrollable-region-focusable` (confirmed via `axe.getRules()`: tags `cat.keyboard, wcag2a, wcag211` — WCAG **2.1.1 Keyboard, Level A** — its own help text is literally "Ensure elements that have scrollable content are accessible by keyboard **in Safari**," i.e. the exact engine behind iOS Safari, the primary mobile browser for AC6's own audience). AC6 *requires* genuine horizontal overflow on mobile by design — this isn't a maybe-it-overflows question, the AC mandates it exists. So a keyboard-only user (external keyboard + VoiceOver/Switch Control on iOS, the device AC6 targets) has no way to reach the "peeking" content at all. **Why CI's Storybook a11y gate passed despite this real rule existing and being enabled:** jsdom (my probe's environment) computes zero real layout, so `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` never differ and the rule structurally cannot fire there — that's a limitation of my own probe, not evidence about the real browser-driven Storybook a11y run. For the *actual* CI check (Playwright-driven, real Chromium, per `test-storybook`), whether the rule fired depends on whether the table's real rendered width exceeds the story's fixed 522px decorator — which I cannot compute without a browser (`MIN_COL_WIDTH` = `calc(4rem+1rem)` = 80px × 6 columns ≈ 480-530px, genuinely borderline, not something I'll claim a verdict on). Regardless of that borderline case, the underlying gap (no `tabIndex`/`role`/`aria-label`) is real and unconditional. 🔴 must-fix, **CONFIRMED** (the missing attributes), **PLAUSIBLE** (that it's what let CI pass), **UNIFORM** (applies to every non-grouped table this PR ships; the `GroupedSizeTable`/Hats path has no scroll wrapper at all, but those tables are narrow enough by construction that it's plausibly moot there).

**h) Fallback `<picture>`/`<img>` alt-text precedence — `sizeGuideContent.tsx:446-451`.**
```tsx
alt={fields.sizeGuideTableLabel ?? fields.imageFallback?.fields.altText ?? fields.imageFallback?.fields.internalTitle ?? ''}
```
This is the strongest finding in this review. Three separate problems, each confirmed against this codebase's own established pattern:
1. `sizeGuideTableLabel` (a *section heading* — Contentful's own help text for this field, in `scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuideTable.js`, literally says "Section heading displayed above the description and table") is checked **before** the image's own purpose-built `altText` field. A heading string front-running the dedicated alt-text field is backwards.
2. It falls through to `imageFallback.fields.internalTitle` — a field the sibling `image.js` content-type explicitly documents as "Internal label shown in the Contentful entry list. **Not rendered on the PDP**." This code renders it as user-facing, AT-announced alt text, contradicting the field's own documented contract.
3. It never checks `fields.imageFallback?.fields.decorative` at all. `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:58` documents this exact field: "Purely decorative — screen readers should skip it (empty alt)." An editor who marks a fallback image decorative still gets it announced to screen readers.
4. **This exact type already has a correct, existing resolver**: `overrides/app/utils/resolveImageEntry.ts:27` — `const alt = image.fields.decorative ? '' : image.fields.altText ?? asset.fields.description ?? asset.fields.title;` — and `SizeGuideTableEntry.fields.imageFallback` is typed as `ImageEntry` (`overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:364`), the *exact same type* `resolveImageEntry` takes. `tsc --noEmit` passing on both branches confirms the types genuinely line up — this was a drop-in call, not an adaptation. Confirmed this utility already has two real consumers (`megaMenuContent/toMegaMenuItem.ts`, `drawer-menu/index.tsx`) per its own doc comment, so this isn't a novel/unused helper, it's an established, ignored one.
WCAG **1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A)**. Axe's `image-alt` rule only checks that an `alt` attribute exists at all (it always does here, even if wrong) — semantically wrong alt content, or a decorative image not getting `alt=""`, is invisible to any automated tool. 🔴 must-fix, **CONFIRMED** (type-level + source-level comparison, not inference), **ONE-OFF** in this PR (one call site) but the general shape ("hand-rolled instead of the shared resolver") is worth watching elsewhere.

**i) Heading-level flattening — `sizeGuideContent.tsx:314-325`.** All of Contentful's `heading-1` through `heading-6` node types render as a literal `<chakra.h2>`, discarding whatever level the content editor actually chose (the schema permits all six per `TABLE_VALIDATIONS`). WCAG 1.3.1 — low real-world likelihood given size-guide copy is typically flat, but a genuine semantic loss if an editor ever nests headings. 🟡 should-fix, **CONFIRMED**, **PLAUSIBLE** impact. Separately — the drawer shell itself (`ZimmPdpDrawer`/`ZimmDrawer`, pre-existing, not part of this PR) renders **no title heading at all** for the tabbed variant (confirmed by reading `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:175-192`: the `title || boxedHeader` branch is false, so neither element renders); the page's own `<h1>` (product name, outside this PR) is presumably the nearest ancestor heading, making the drawer content's first `<h2>` a valid one-level nesting, not a skip. No violation there, just documenting why I didn't also flag it.

## 5. AC5 (responsive) / AC6 (mobile peek) — reasoned from CSS, not measured

**AC6** (mobile peek + scrollability hint): the mechanism is plausible — `MIN_COL_WIDTH` forces cells wider than a narrow viewport can hold, `overflowX: auto` produces genuine horizontal scroll, and the `_after` gradient fades the cut-off content toward white rather than a hard clip, which is a reasonable reading of "sizes... peek out." I have not measured this in a browser and won't claim a pixel verdict. The gap I can state with confidence is (g) above: the scrollable region itself has no keyboard affordance, which undermines AC6 specifically for keyboard-only mobile users, independent of whether the visual peek renders correctly.

**AC5** ("fully responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop"): the drawer's own width-switching (`mobile`/`tablet`/`large` variants, `useBreakpointValue`) is pre-existing infrastructure this PR doesn't touch, and `sizeGuideContent.tsx`'s layout (`VStack`/`Flex`, no fixed pixel widths on its own containers) should reflow generically regardless of the drawer's resulting width. What I can say with confidence, though, is that **nothing in this PR's own verification surface ever exercises more than one width**: both `zimmTable/index.stories.tsx` and `sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx` decorate every single story with the identical fixed `<Box width="522px">` — a value that doesn't correspond to any of the three named breakpoint states (mobile ≈100vw, tablet ≈80% of 768-1279px, desktop ≈50% of ≥1280px per the drawer's own comment). Combined with Playwright being skipped (per gates.md) and jsdom/Vitest being structurally unable to compute real layout, **no test or story in this PR provides any evidence that the three responsive states actually work** — the claim rests entirely on the pre-existing drawer shell plus generic flex behaviour, unverified by anything this PR shipped. I'd flag this as a verification gap against AC5 as literally written, not a confirmed functional break.

The gloves table's "SHORT GLOVES / LONG GLOVES" grouped-header layout (`columnSpan`+`subColumns`, built specifically for this per the recipe's own comment) is never actually produced by `richTextTableToZimmProps` — worth knowing before treating AC2's gloves coverage as proven by the `ZimmTable`-level `WithSubColumns` story, which exercises the atom directly, not the real content pipeline.

---

## What I tried to falsify

- Assumed the row-label column must be a `<th>` given the "generic data table atom" framing in the doc comment — read the actual render branch and confirmed it's a `<td>`, then reproduced it two ways (static grep + live axe probe) rather than trusting the doc comment's framing.
- Assumed `TABLET_MIN_WIDTH` was a defensible one-off given media queries can't consume `var()` — checked whether the codebase's real answer to that problem (import the JS constant instead) was already established elsewhere, and found 15+ instances of exactly that pattern, making this file the outlier.
- Assumed the CI-passing Storybook a11y gate meant no real table/scroll/image defect existed — built an actual axe-core probe against the real installed version instead of taking the green check at face value, and used it to explain (with rule tags and `enabled` flags, not memory) precisely why each defect passed.
- Assumed the alt-text fallback chain was merely a stylistic ordering choice — cross-checked it against the Contentful schema's own field-help text and against `resolveImageEntry.ts`'s type signature, which turned a "maybe backwards" hunch into a confirmed drop-in-utility-not-used bug.
- Assumed `gates.md`'s "0 in this PR's files" claim for `audit:tokens` might be stale — re-ran it myself in `wt113`, got an identical 6/6 unacknowledged count, then read the script's scan-root logic directly rather than trusting either the doc or the count alone.

## What I could not verify

- Any real pixel measurement — table overflow width vs. the 522px story decorator, actual drawer widths at `tablet`/`large` variants, actual rendered focus-ring colour/contrast on `NavItem`. No browser available, stated per finding above.
- Whether axe-core's `scrollable-region-focusable` rule actually fired (or would fire) in the real Playwright-driven Storybook a11y CI run — my jsdom probe cannot compute real overflow at all (a jsdom limitation, not a repo one), so I can only reason about it, not reproduce it.
- Real screen-reader behaviour (VoiceOver/NVDA/JAWS table-navigation-mode announcements) — reasoned from WCAG technique documentation and axe rule semantics, not from an actual AT session.
- Whether `td-has-header`'s "larger than 3×3" size gate was the specific reason it didn't fire on my fixture, versus the column-already-has-a-`th` reasoning I gave — I confirmed the *outcome* (zero violations) empirically but didn't trace axe-core's internal rule-evaluation source to confirm *which* internal branch skipped it.
- Anything about `useSizeGuide.ts`/`useContentful.ts` (AC4's Contentful fallback-order logic) or unit-conversion correctness (AC3) — explicitly out of my assigned angle, left to whichever other tester covers logic/data-mapping.

## What Marcel is missing

The alt-text finding (4h) is the one I'd escalate above the others: it's not specific to this PR's pattern, it's a **regression against an already-solved problem** — `resolveImageEntry.ts` exists, is typed identically, and is already used by two other components, so any future Contentful-image consumer that doesn't grep for it first is one PR away from repeating exactly this (wrong precedence + ignored `decorative` flag + a "not rendered" field leaking to production). Worth a lint/convention note ("any `ImageEntry`-typed field resolves through `resolveImageEntry`, no exceptions") rather than relying on each PR's reviewer to independently notice the type match, the way I did here.</result>

content.text:
## Full review — PR #113, SFCC-102

State re-checked just now: OPEN, head `60dc243b`, `BLOCKED`, `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. Nothing has moved since I started.

**One correction to what I told you earlier.** I said the a11y gate misses the scroll violation because "the stories render wide enough that nothing overflows." The precise reason is different and it changes the fix: the story decorator is 522px with 16px padding, so 490px usable, and the **widest table in any story fixture is 5 columns × 80px = 400px**. Real Contentful content is 7 columns = 560px. The gate passes because the fixtures are narrower than the content they stand in for. So the ask isn't just `tabIndex`, it's also a fixture that matches real column count, or the gate won't catch the next one either.

### Gates

| Gate | Base | Head | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | |
| `lint` | 1297 | **1293** | 4 fewer warnings |
| `audit:tokens` | 6 | 6, none his | no change |
| `test` | 105 / 1536 | **108 / 1599** | +63 tests, all pass |

Unit tests and Storybook a11y genuinely executed. **Playwright and BrowserStack were skipped.**

### Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore

**1. Toggling INCH leaves two thirds of the gloves guide in centimetres.** CONFIRMED live · in-scope
`sizeGuideContent.tsx:398-404`. Gloves links three `sizeGuideTable` entries; only the first has `hasCmInchToggle: true`. Unit state is held per entry, so the one toggle that renders can't reach the other two. Shopper clicks INCH, sees "Length 26.3", reads it as inches. It's 26.3cm. AC3 says *all* measurements update. Hats works because it's one entry with three table nodes.

**2. The schema he wrote enables content the renderer he wrote silently deletes.** CONFIRMED · in-scope
`sizeGuideTable.js:7-21` enables lists, blockquote and embedded entries; `sizeGuideContent.tsx:341` returns `null` for all of them. The section survives the empty-section filter (the text extractor sees the words) and renders as a blank gap. Same for underline/strikethrough marks, which the schema allows and line 334 ignores.

**3. An unpublished Contentful asset crashes the render.** CONFIRMED · in-scope
`useContentful.ts:76-78` resolves Asset links with `if (linked)` and **no else**, unlike the Entry branch below it. The stub survives with no `.fields`. Then `sizeGuideContent.tsx:412` does `asset?.fields.file.url`. The optional chain guards absence, not a stub. No error boundary on this path. One reviewer reproduced it by executing the real function.

**4. The scrollable tables have no keyboard affordance.** CONFIRMED live · in-scope
axe against the live drawer: 1 serious violation (`scrollable-region-focusable`, 2 nodes) at 375px, 0 at 1440px. WCAG 2.1.1. Works in Chrome 127+ by accident; Safari and Firefox don't.

**5. Row labels are `<td>`, and no `<th>` has `scope`.** CONFIRMED · in-scope
"Bust" and "Waist" are row headers marked up as data cells. axe's `td-has-header` doesn't fire because column 0 already has a `<th>` at the top, which satisfies the structural check without describing anything. WCAG 1.3.1. No table has an accessible name either.

**6. `unique: true` on `key` forbids what the hook and three of its tests assume.** CONFIRMED · in-scope
`sizeGuide.js:24`. But `useSizeGuide.test.ts` builds two entries sharing `size-guide__womens_dresses` to prove region precedence. Contentful will refuse to save the second. Region filtering came in the final commit and wasn't reconciled with the schema already written.

**7. The fallback image's alt text prefers the section heading, then a field marked "not rendered".** CONFIRMED, latent · in-scope
`sizeGuideContent.tsx:446-451` does `sizeGuideTableLabel ?? altText ?? internalTitle`. `internalTitle` is documented in `types/contentful.ts:53` as "Editor-facing label only, not rendered". `decorative` is never checked. `resolveImageEntry.ts` already does all three correctly, takes the exact same type, and has two existing consumers. **Caveat: none of the ten sample products renders a fallback image, so nobody sees this today.**

**8. `CM`, `INCH`, `Unit` and `Category` are hardcoded English** across 11 locales, in a file where "Coming Soon" three lines away goes through `FormattedMessage`. There's no written rule, only unanimous precedent.

**9. `TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = '48em'` retypes `breakpoints.md`** — 15+ other files import it instead.

**10. Two thirds of `ZimmTable` is unreachable.** `labelless`, `bordered`, `subColumns`, `columnSpan`, `spans` are used only by the atom's own story. Gloves and hats, which the JSDoc says they're for, already render correctly through the standard branch.

**Small:** misplaced JSDoc at `sizeGuideContent.tsx:86-99` leaves the exported `isGroupedTableNode` undocumented; `productInfo.ts:58`'s `c_sizeGuide` example says `"womens-dresses"` but the real value is `clothing-op-4`; the CM/INCH buttons get the browser's blue focus ring instead of the site's dark one; both Tier 2 notification checkboxes in his own PR body are unticked.

### Yours, not the PR's

Clothing and denim body measurements are **authored in inches under a CM label** — the ticket's reference image says Bust should be 79/84/89/94/99/104, live shows 31/33/35/37/39/41. Content team. · Confluence assigns `__en` to the US; `en` is Australia in `config/sites.js`. BA. · "Find My Size" is a visible on-page link that opens "Coming Soon"; the ticket contradicts itself about whether it should exist at all. BA. · SFCC-674 owns "Contentful Size Guide content type" and is still Ready For Review while this PR ships its own copy.

### What nobody verified

Design fidelity beyond the ticket's reference image — no Figma node, so spacing, type ramp, hover/disabled states, tablet, and the grouped "Layout 3" variant are unchecked. Whether the Size Guide tab renders fully empty for a product with neither a guide nor `sizeFit` (couldn't find one). Whether the content types are installed in any environment above dev. Real screen-reader behaviour. And Playwright never ran on this PR at all.

### Killed before they reached you

Six: EU-FR showing no guide (modal intercepted the click), no focus ring at all (`.focus()` artifact), hooks after a conditional throw (already on develop), `richText.tsx` being a duplicate renderer (it parses HTML, different thing), `.claude/registry` hiding a Tier 1 gate (it doesn't), and one reviewer's claim that a bare-language locale key can't be produced (it can — I measured AU sending `__en`; another reviewer got it right and contradicted them).

content.text:
Right. Plain version, consequence first.

## The seven that are Jhoan's to fix

**1. Gloves shows centimetres while the button says inches.**
A customer on a gloves product clicks INCH. The top table changes. The two below it don't, and nothing says so. They read "Length 26.3" as inches. It's 26.3 centimetres, so they're off by a factor of two and a half and they order the wrong size.
*Why:* each block on the page remembers its own unit separately. The gloves guide is assembled from three separate content records and only the first one was set up with a toggle. So the single INCH button on screen only talks to its own block and physically cannot reach the other two. Hats works fine because it's one record containing three tables.
*Fix:* one toggle for the whole guide, or make sure every record with measurements gets its own. That's his design call, not mine.

**2. Bulleted lists disappear.**
A content editor writes the "how to measure" steps as a bullet list, publishes, and the page shows an empty gap. No error, no warning, nothing in the console.
*Why:* the Contentful field is configured to allow lists, numbered lists, quotes and embedded blocks. The code that draws that content only knows headings and paragraphs and throws everything else away. The empty gap appears because a different bit of code asks "does this section contain any words?" — a list does contain words, so the section is kept, and then nothing gets drawn inside it. Both files are new in this PR, so it's his schema disagreeing with his renderer.
*Fix:* either stop allowing those types in the field, or draw them.

**3. Unpublishing an image in Contentful breaks the product page.**
Not the size guide. The page.
*Why:* when content is fetched, pointers to images get swapped for the real image. If the image is missing, the code leaves the pointer sitting there instead of removing it — and it does remove missing pointers of the other kind, two lines below, so the asymmetry is accidental. The page then asks that pointer for its file URL and a pointer has no file. The `?.` in his line guards against the image being *missing*, not against it being *a dead pointer*. There's no error boundary anywhere near this, so it takes the page with it.
*Fix:* one more `?.`.

**4. Keyboard users can't scroll the table sideways on a phone.**
The table is wider than the screen by 249 pixels and you swipe it. Someone on a keyboard has no way to reach the columns off the right edge.
*Why:* the scrolling box isn't in the tab order and has no name. Chrome started handling this automatically last year so it works there by luck; Safari and Firefox don't.
*The part worth knowing:* the automated accessibility check should have caught this and didn't. Not because the check is weak — it genuinely fails builds. Because the test fixtures are narrower than the real content. Widest fixture is 5 columns; production is 7. Nothing ever overflows in the test, so the check never has anything to find.
*Fix:* make the box focusable and name it, and widen the fixture so the check can do its job next time.

**5. Screen readers lose the row context.**
Someone hears "33" with no indication it's the Bust measurement for size 0. For a size guide, that's the only thing it exists to communicate.
*Why:* the first cell of each row — Bust, Waist, Hips — is marked as an ordinary data cell rather than a row heading. The automated check passes because the column above already has a heading, which satisfies the letter of the rule while missing its point.
*Fix:* make the label cell a header cell.

**6. The schema forbids something the code and three of its tests rely on.**
Nothing breaks today. But the region feature is dead on arrival, and the next person who tries to make a US-specific clothing guide will hit a wall they can't get past.
*Why:* the code supports two versions of the same guide, one region-specific and one default. Contentful will refuse to save the second one, because the schema marks that key unique. Region filtering went in on the last commit, probably answering CodeRabbit, and wasn't checked against the schema he'd written earlier in the same PR. Three tests currently prove behaviour that can't exist.
*Fix:* drop the unique rule or drop the region axis. That's a decision, not a patch.

**7. Wrong alt text on fallback images.**
Nobody sees this today — no live guide uses a picture instead of a table. It's a trap for later.
*Why:* the alt text is assembled by hand. It prefers the section heading over the image's own alt text, then falls back to an internal CMS label that the type definition explicitly says is never rendered, and it ignores the "this image is decorative" flag entirely. A helper that does all three correctly already exists, is already used in two other components, and takes exactly this data type.
*Fix:* call the helper.

## Three smaller ones

**8.** "CM", "INCH" and the hidden screen-reader labels are hardcoded English across 11 locales. Three lines away in the same file, "Coming Soon" goes through the translation system. To be fair to him, there's no written rule about this in the repo — only unanimous practice.

**9.** `48em` is typed out fresh instead of imported from the design foundation. Fifteen other files import it. If the designer moves the tablet breakpoint, this file won't follow.

**10.** He built three layout modes into the new table component. The size guide only ever uses one. The other two were built for gloves and hats, which already render correctly through the normal path.

## The two that aren't his

**The clothing and denim numbers are wrong in the CMS.** The design reference on the ticket says Bust in centimetres should be 79/84/89/94/99/104. The site shows 31/33/35/37/39/41, which are the inch values. So the content was typed in inches and labelled cm, and then the INCH button converts it *again* down to 12.2. Mens is correct, which proves his conversion code is fine. There's a field in the schema that would fix it and no entry uses it. Content team.

**Confluence tells authors to use `__en` for the US size guides.** In our config, `en` is Australia — the US is `en-US`. So a US-specific guide authored exactly as the doc instructs would appear in Australia and never in the US. Nobody has authored one yet, so it hasn't bitten. BA or whoever owns that page.

Now the three decisions:
